title: Two children suffice for target avoidance, even with permanent genders

plain_language.question: How small can the child cap be while a permanent-gender population avoids a prescribed infinite binary target?
plain_language.what_we_learned: The exact threshold is two; an avoider exists exactly when the cap is at least two and the target is not eventually periodic.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Use the same three-root, two-child underlying graph for every such target, changing only genders, while retaining inspecies and specieslike guarantees.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: Three roots are not proved minimal, and this does not introduce a new line-graph operation or empirical population model.

exact_statement_and_scope: For every natural cap and binary infinite word s, there exist an infinite retained vertex set, an actual eligible permanent-binary-gender population with at most cap children per vertex and finite actual roots, and avoidance of s from every starting vertex, iff cap≥2 and s is not eventually periodic. Nonroots have parents of each gender and chronology/finite-prefix conditions are retained. Below two no eligible infinite population exists. The directed line graph of the original P_s has exactly three roots, exactly two children per vertex and two opposite-gender parents at every nonroot, with full infinite-word language preserved without a shifted first letter. The unlabelled graph is fixed across targets; only genders change. The same actual retained witness is specieslike, an inspecies and reflective. Three-root optimality is not part of the result.
